Subject: Deployment mode selection & migration plan – Lumina Labs

Hi Evan / Sasha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared plan and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of needs
- High throughput for real-time inference (peak ~200 req/s, average 60 req/s)
- P95 latency target ~200–300ms for single-turn generation
- PHI in prompts/outputs — HIPAA considerations and strict access controls
- Migration from an existing self-hosted GPU cluster + partial usage of OpenAI for R&D

Deployment modes we discussed
1) Hosted API: fastest to get started, Redwood-managed, good for PoC and initial integration.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput, better cost at scale, data isolation within our infra.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed private control plane and KMS — recommended for regulated production.

Recommended next steps
- Please confirm which deployment mode(s) you want us to prioritize for timelines and pricing. If you’re unsure, we recommend: start with Hosted API for a 2–4 week PoC, then move to Dedicated for production and evaluate Private for strict PHI requirements.
- Connor (cc) will follow up with a migration checklist and an initial technical plan (data flow, tokenization compatibility, auth).
- If acceptable, let’s schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week to map the migration path and SLA/throughput sizing.

Attachments: Redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf (high-level), SOC2-attestation.pdf

Thanks —

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. That matches our internal notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Throughput: the 200 req/s peak comes from our customer-facing inference for document summarization during business hours. We can likely tolerate a brief warmup period during bursts, but the KV/cache behavior matters.
- PHI: Yes — we need SOC2 + evidence of KMS integration. Our security team will validate technical controls.
- Migration: we currently run a mix: an internal self-hosted GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100s) for heavy models and call OpenAI for lighter workloads. The plan we prefer is to move model serving away from the cluster over 3 months while keeping a fallback to the cluster during the transition.

Questions:
1) For Dedicated — can you share expected commit sizes (GPUs / vCPU equivalents) and a rough monthly cost estimate for 4x A100-ish capacity?
2) For Private VPC — what is the onboarding timeline? We may need air-gapped/on-prem options for a subset of regulated customers.

Sasha and I are available next Tue/Wed afternoon PT for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks,
Evan Clark
VP Engineering, Lumina Labs
evan@luminalabs.com

From: Connor Obrien <connor@redwoodinference.com>

Evan / Sasha —

Thanks for the detail — we can run a practical migration path that minimizes risk. A few technical notes and timeline expectations: 

Migration recommendation
- Phase 1 (PoC, 2–4 weeks): Hosted API with request routing and prefix caching. This verifies integration, prompt/response correctness, and latency at your typical load. No infra commit required.
- Phase 2 (staging, 4–6 weeks): Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool). We mirror traffic and evaluate throughput, autoscaling, and KV cache hit rates. We can set up a cross-traffic experiment with your cluster as fallback.
- Phase 3 (production, 2–8 weeks + planning): Private VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads if required. Onboarding depends on network approvals and KMS integration; typical timeline 4–8 weeks for VPC, longer for fully air-gapped installs.

Technical considerations
- Tokenization and model variants: We’ll run a token-compatibility pass and diff outputs for a representative prompt set. For now assume model parity with your current model family.
- KV/prefix caching: Redwood can do prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token compute; cache TTLs and invalidation are configurable and important for your burst profile.
- Fallbacks: We support smart routing — if Redwood Dedicated reaches capacity, requests can fall back to your cluster or to a lighter hosted variant.

Commit sizing & rough pricing (very high level)
- 4x A100-equivalent Dedicated pool: rough starting commit $XXK–$YYK/month (depends on discounts and support). I’ll get a formal quote from our pricing team after we lock target QPS and latency SLOs.

Attachments: migration-checklist.xlsx (initial tech tasks & owners)

Connor Obrien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor@redwoodinference.com
